modules.ipa-plus.chart.ipa.diacritics.gr: voiceless
A segment that is normally voiced has absent or reduced periodic vocal-fold vibration.
voiced
Marks vocal-fold vibration in a segment that is normally voiceless.
aspirated
Consonant release is followed by audible airflow noise or an extended period of glottal opening.
more rounded
Increases rounding relative to the base sound's typical lip shape.
less rounded
Reduces rounding relative to the base sound.
advanced
The primary lingual place moves forward relative to the base sound.
retracted
The primary lingual place moves backward relative to the base sound.
centralized
The vowel's tongue position moves from front or back toward the center.
mid-centralized
The vowel approaches the center of vowel space in both height and backness.
syllabic
Makes the marked segment function as a syllable nucleus.
non-syllabic
The marked vowel or resonant does not independently function as a syllable nucleus.
rhoticity
Marks rhotic quality in a vowel without specifying a unique tongue shape.
breathy voiced
Vocal-fold vibration is accompanied by prominent airflow leakage noise.
creaky voiced
Marks creaky properties of lower-frequency or irregular vocal-fold vibration, rather than generic roughness.
linguolabial
The tongue tip or blade contacts or approaches the upper lip.
labialized
The primary articulation is accompanied by extra rounding or lip constriction.
palatalized
The primary articulation is accompanied by tongue-body raising toward the hard palate.
velarized
The primary articulation is accompanied by the back of the tongue approaching the soft palate.
pharyngealized
The primary articulation is accompanied by pharyngeal constriction. Describe the mechanism for the actual material.
velarized or pharyngealized
A diacritic through the letter broadly denotes velarization or pharyngealization; use a dedicated marker when the mechanism needs to be explicit.
raised
Raises vowel tongue position or increases consonant constriction.
lowered
Lowers vowel tongue position or decreases consonant constriction.
advanced tongue root
Describes an advanced tongue-root setting; it is not equivalent to advancing the whole tongue body.
retracted tongue root
Describes a retracted tongue-root setting; it is not simply a back vowel.
dental
Articulatory contact moves toward the teeth.
apical
Specifies the tongue tip as the active articulator.
laminal
Specifies the tongue blade as the active articulator, distinct from apical articulation.
nasalized
Oral airflow also escapes through the nose, usually due to velum lowering.
nasal release
A stop's oral closure is released by opening the nasal passage.
lateral release
Air passes along the tongue sides during stop release.
no audible release
No separate release burst is heard at the end of closure. This does not prove that the closure was never released.
voiceless above
For a base letter with a descender, place the devoicing ring above to avoid overlapping its strokes.

modules.ipa-plus.chart.extipa.diacritics: Diacritics
Position, airflow and articulatory degree. Select standalone markers first, or insert complete items labelled as examples.
labial spreading
The lips spread sideways, distinguishing lip-shape changes on the same base.
strong articulation
Articulatory action is stronger than the reference realization of the same sound type.
weak articulation
Articulatory action is weaker than the reference realization of the same sound type; this does not directly mean lower volume.
partially denasal
A nasal has reduced nasal resonance or airflow relative to its typical form; retain the meaning of partial.
fricative nasal escape
Nasal airflow escape with audible friction.
velopharyngeal friction
Velopharyngeal friction accompanies the base sound.
main gesture offset right
The primary articulation shifts right of the speaker's midline.
main gesture offset left
The primary articulation shifts left of the speaker's midline.
whistled articulation
A narrow airstream creates a distinct whistle quality, unlike ordinary fricative noise.
reiteration
Marks successive repetition of the same closure or gesture; place between the repeated symbols.
ingressive airflow
Placed beside a segment to mark inward airflow.
sliding articulation
A continuous slide from one place or sound value to another, with an arrow between the bases.

Final partial devoicing: the ending portion lacks vocal-fold vibration; parentheses specify the affected span.

Final partial voicing: vocal-fold vibration occurs only in the ending portion.

Enclosures mark uncertain identification; distinguish parenthesized silent articulation from double-parenthesized extraneous noise.
indeterminate sound
A sound was observed but its phonetic properties cannot be reliably identified.
indeterminate consonant
The sound can be reliably classified only as consonant; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate obstruent
The sound can be reliably classified only as obstruent; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate fricative
The sound can be reliably classified only as fricative; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate liquid
The sound can be reliably classified only as liquid; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate glide
The sound can be reliably classified only as glide; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate nasal
The sound can be reliably classified only as nasal; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate plosive
The sound can be reliably classified only as plosive; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate rhotic or resonant
The sound can be reliably classified only as rhotic or resonant; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate sibilant
The sound can be reliably classified only as sibilant; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate tone or accent
The sound can be reliably classified only as tone / accent; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate nasal vowel
The sound can be reliably classified only as nasalized vowel; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate click
The sound can be reliably classified only as click; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate syllable
The sound can be reliably classified only as syllable; a more precise phonetic value cannot be determined.
indeterminate span (text substitute)
Retains uncertainty in a provisionally transcribed stretch.
silent articulation
Articulatory movement is observed without a corresponding audible speech sound.
extraneous noise
Place descriptions of extra sounds, such as coughing, or unidentified stretches in double parentheses.

modules.ipa-plus.chart.extipa.other.grou: apical r
An r-like approximant whose main active articulator is the tongue tip.
bunched r (molar r)
Rhotic quality produced by bunching the tongue. Rhoticity alone does not establish retroflexion.
laminal fricative
The tongue blade forms the principal constriction; realizations may include a lowered tongue tip.
laminal fricative
A voiced laminal sibilant; realizations may include a lowered tongue tip.
lateral fricated release
The release of d includes a voiced lateral fricative component.
lateral fricated release
The release of k includes a voiceless velar lateral fricative component.
lateral and median release
The release of t has simultaneous central and lateral friction.
lateral and median release
The release of d has simultaneous voiced central and lateral friction.
voiceless linguolabial affricate
A linguolabial stop releases continuously into linguolabial friction. The tie denotes one combined articulatory unit.
voiced linguolabial affricate
A linguolabial stop releases continuously into a voiced linguolabial fricative.
voiceless velodorsal plosive
A special velar closure involving a reversed dorsal gesture, distinguished from ordinary k by a dedicated extended letter.
voiced velodorsal plosive
The voiced counterpart of this special velodorsal closure.
velodorsal nasal
The corresponding special velodorsal closure with nasal airflow.
sublaminal lower-alveolar percussive
The underside of the tongue strikes the lower alveolar region, distinct from an ordinary apical alveolar stop.
alveolar click with sublaminal percussive release
Alveolar click release combined with a sublaminal percussive component.
buccal interdental trill (raspberry)
Air in the cheeks drives interdental trilling, termed raspberry in the original chart.
t with bidental aspiration
Aspiration of t passes through a channel between upper and lower teeth; the bidental marker modifies the aspiration component.
sound with no available symbol
Use an asterisk for an identified unusual sound with no available symbol, and add a written explanation.
